t: A pocket USB tool for flashing and fixing code on small boards.
steps: Buy the Debug Probe from a store such as Adafruit, SparkFun, PiShop.us or CanaKit.
Install VS Code and the Raspberry Pi Pico extension, which bundles OpenOCD, GDB, and the compiler.
Connect a Pico to its own USB power and join the grounds first.
Plug the D cable into the Pico debug pins and the U cable into its serial pins.
Plug the probe into your computer with the included USB cable.
Open the blink example in the Pico extension and start a debug session.
Set a breakpoint and step through the code line by line.
Update the probe firmware by holding BOOTSEL and dragging the newest UF2 onto it.
meta: Open Board. From $12. Easy to find.
